f2_direct_observations: WP804 already encodes explicit GOAL versus ABSTAIN decisions.
WP804 labels an exact goal only when declared public evidence uniquely identifies one candidate.
WP804 requires ABSTAIN when public evidence is non-identifying and seals evaluator labels after policy inference.
WP804 GoalInferenceScore is currently boolean correctness over decision plus exact goal id; non-identifiable cases do not preserve the full compatible-goal set in the score object.

external_primary_sources.title: Reward Identification in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
external_primary_sources.finding: Identifiability is a first-class property of inverse inference; identifiable and non-identifiable model instances require explicit distinction.

external_primary_sources.title: Towards Theoretical Understanding of Inverse Reinforcement Learning
external_primary_sources.finding: When a unique reward is not identifiable, the feasible set of rewards compatible with observations is itself the meaningful inferential object.

external_primary_sources.title: Learning true objectives: Linear algebraic characterizations of identifiability in inverse reinforcement learning
external_primary_sources.finding: Multiple objectives can explain the same behavior; prior/model structure changes identifiability and should not be conflated with observation evidence.

external_primary_sources.title: An LP-Based Approach for Goal Recognition as Planning
external_primary_sources.finding: Goal recognition under partial/noisy observations naturally reasons over the set of candidate goals compatible with observations.

external_primary_sources.title: Active Goal Recognition
external_primary_sources.finding: An observer can act or sense specifically to reduce uncertainty among hypothesized goals, so ambiguity structure can have downstream action value.

external_primary_sources.title: AgentAbstain: Do LLM Agents Know When Not to Act?
external_primary_sources.finding: Paired should-act/should-abstain evaluation exposes an agent capability distinct from ordinary task success and detects unsafe post-hoc abstention.

e1_conclusion.supported_residual_hypothesis: For non-identifiable cases, retaining a compact public-compatible goal-hypothesis set may provide useful ambiguity structure for later Hyperposition and Epistemic Action Selection without granting goal authority.
e1_conclusion.counterhypothesis: WP804 is intentionally a bounded binary falsifier; preserving the ambiguity set could duplicate Hyperposition, add benchmark complexity, or leak evaluator semantics into cognition with no measurable downstream gain.

next_discriminator: Map whether a benchmark-only compatible-goal-set/ambiguity profile can be computed entirely from the same public ObservationView and CandidateGoal inputs, remain authority-free, and enable a paired downstream information-seeking falsifier that binary ABSTAIN cannot distinguish.
